title: Web Performance Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Web Performance course.

entries.name: Measure before changing code
entries.summary: A performance measurement is a clue about a real task.

example.code:
Choose one page and one task.
Record the device and network setting.
Load it several times.
Write down what feels slow.
Change one cause and repeat the same test.

entries.name: Know the three web vital ideas
entries.summary: Core Web Vitals describe loading, response to input and visual stability.

example.code:
LCP: When the largest main content becomes visible.
INP: How quickly the page shows a response to interactions.
CLS: How much visible content unexpectedly moves.

entries.name: Give images their size
entries.summary: Image width and height tell the browser the picture's shape before it finishes loading.

entries.name: Load lower images later
entries.summary: Lazy loading delays some images until they are near the visible area.

entries.name: Offer an image that fits
entries.summary: Responsive image sources let the browser choose a suitable image size.

entries.name: Keep early scripts from blocking HTML
entries.summary: A deferred classic script downloads while HTML is read and runs after parsing.

entries.name: Load optional code when needed
entries.summary: Dynamic import can load a JavaScript module when a feature is used.

entries.name: Avoid repeating layout work
entries.summary: Reading layout after each style change can make the browser repeatedly calculate positions.

entries.name: Schedule a visual update
entries.summary: requestAnimationFrame asks the browser to run a visual update before a future paint.

entries.name: Use a font fallback
entries.summary: A fallback font shows readable words while a web font loads.

entries.name: Understand browser caching
entries.summary: A cache keeps a response so it may be reused.

example.code:
For a versioned asset such as app.a1b2c3.js, a static host may send:
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

For HTML that changes, use a policy that lets the browser check for updates.

entries.name: Keep a performance checklist
entries.summary: A useful performance budget sets limits that matter for the page.

example.code:
List important pages and tasks.
Track total transferred image and script sizes.
Check a slower device and network.
Review LCP, INP and CLS evidence.
Keep accessibility and readable content in every check.
Repeat after large new features.
